cards.title: Greg Wise on Failed IVF and Existential Crisis
cards.body: The actor and Emma Thompson faced devastating grief after unsuccessful IVF cycles while trying for a second child. Two decades later, Wise reflects on how the experience challenged their identities and relationship during this deeply painful period.

cards.title: Parental Attitudes Toward Music and Parenting Styles
cards.body: Parents who judge their children's musical tastes harshly may miss opportunities to connect with them. Learning to appreciate what your kids enjoy, even if it differs from your preferences, can strengthen family bonds.

cards.title: Shared Parenting Responsibilities and Modern Fatherhood
cards.body: Basketball player LaMelo Ball's public avoidance of diaper duty reflects outdated attitudes about parenting roles. Equal participation in childcare is essential for modern families and children's development.

cards.title: Family Traditions After Empty Nest
cards.body: Creating meaningful rituals like making jam together helps maintain family bonds after children move out. These yearly traditions provide continuity and connection across generations.

cards.title: The 3-Minute Rule for Difficult Family Conversations
cards.body: The first three minutes of a hard conversation significantly influence its outcome. Research offers practical strategies for timing and tone to improve family discussions.

cards.title: Pregnancy Loss After Infertility Creates Compounded Grief
cards.body: When pregnancy finally arrives after years of trying, loss carries grief far deeper than the miscarriage itself. Parents must process years of hope and anticipation alongside the immediate loss.

cards.title: Social Skills Development Essential for Young Adults
cards.body: Recent graduates without adequate social skills face employment instability later in life. College provides the last opportunity for students to build crucial interpersonal competencies before entering the workforce.

cards.title: Preventing Dementia: Steps Families Can Take
cards.body: While there's no cure for dementia or Alzheimer's, research shows prevention strategies can help. Families should explore evidence-based approaches to support cognitive health across generations.
